label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
@Mikaela sorry for the slow reply, been flat out. Short version: we’ve got on alright and I’d do it again, but I’m not going to talk you into it. Grant, you might want a read too.

We’re 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. Started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept, just after mating started. We skip Tues, Thurs and Sat arvos plus Sunday arvo, so four once-a-days a week. Mornings are 5.15 every day, same as always.

Production: milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep had said expect 8–10%, so we’ve done better than that, but 6% is still 6%. It’s not free.

Cells: SCC jumped from 110k to about 180k over the first three weeks. That gave me a bit of a turn. Back around 135k now but I’m still watching it. Your vet and the Fonterra rep are probably both half right — the real version is somewhere in the middle. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days or it bites you. That’s the bit I’d stress most.

Lameness is way down though. We’ve got 4 on the lame list now versus 11 this time last year. Our long walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km, so the arvos off have made a real difference.

Cows came round quicker than I thought too — about 4 days of bellowing at the gate then they were fine. Kieran, our 2IC, said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. That’s worth a lot.

The bad bit: we had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo and I didn’t spot it till next morning. Lost a quarter. That one still stings, and it’s why I’d say don’t go into it unless you’ve got a proper routine for checking cows on those afternoons.

But honestly, I wouldn’t go back. The hours alone are worth the 6%. Dave and me went to Hamilton to see the grandkids the first Sunday arvo we skipped — first Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years. That’s not nothing.

If Tom’s knees are bad, the arvos off will help more than anything. And if your young fella is already talking about leaving because of hours, this might buy you a bit of time there too.

Come find me at the field day at the Kerrisons on the 19th and I’ll show you our shed roster and the numbers. Or just ring me if you want — easier than texting. No rush.
